standard_prerequisites.name: Tensor products commute with finite direct sums
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used for the top arrow of the counted diagram (lines 21551-21557)
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the top horizontal map an isomorphism for a finite free module, which is what the diagram chase consumes.

standard_prerequisites.name: Right exactness of the tensor product
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the surjection from a finite free module onto M into a surjection between the tensored products.

core_obligations: Prove (1) implies (2): choose a surjection from a finite free module onto M, draw the commutative square, note that the top arrow is an isomorphism because tensor products commute with finite direct sums, and conclude that the bottom arrow is surjective by a diagram chase (proof lines 21548-21559).
The implications (2) to (3) to (4) are immediate specialisations of the families involved (proof line 21562).

Prove (4) implies (1): using the diagonal element of M indexed by M itself, write it as a finite sum in the image of the canonical map, apply the projection to the x-th factor, and read off a finite generating set of M (proof lines 21562-21572).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a finite free presentation and chase the square to get one implication (proof lines 21547-21559).
Specialise the family in the other direction and use the diagonal element to recover generators (proof lines 21561-21573).
difficulty_reason: The proposition characterises finitely generated modules by the surjectivity of the canonical map from M tensor a direct product of modules to the product of the tensored modules, in four equivalent forms (statement lines 21532-21545). The proof does not estimate cardinalities of generating sets: it reduces the first implication to a finite free presentation whose square has an isomorphism on top by commutation of tensor products with finite direct sums, and proves the reverse implication by feeding in the diagonal element of M indexed by M, whose finiteness as a sum in the image directly produces a finite generating set (proof lines 21547-21573). Deciding to use the diagonal element is the step that carries the reverse implication. H2.
